deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous and next pages show Gauss working on the cubic (order-3) transformation of the elliptic differential dx/sqrt((1-xx)(1-ss xx)) by the rational substitution x = t(α+βt²)/(γ+δt²). The normalisation x=1 at t=1 gives α+β = γ+δ. The previous page ended with two conditions linking the coefficients to the modulus s and an auxiliary constant c:
(1) γγ/αα = (ββ/δδ)ss + cc·2(α+β)/(3β+3γ−α−δ)
(2) γγ/αα + (ββ/δδ)ss = (αα+ββ−2γδ)((γ−δ)²−(α−β)²ss)/(αγ+αδ+βδ−3βγ).
This page simplifies both conditions with the ratios p = γ/α and q = β/δ. The lower half turns to theta series and cube roots of unity, i.e. the three conjugate values that arise in an order-3 transformation.

A. Condition (1).
Gauss restates (1) as γγ/αα = (ββ/δδ)ss + 2(α+β)cc/(3(β+γ)−(α+δ)).
With γ = αp and β = δq the fraction becomes 2(α+δq)/(3(δq+αp)−α−δ).
The normalisation α+β = γ+δ reads αp+δ = α+δq, i.e. α(p−1) = δ(q−1). So α : δ = (q−1) : (p−1).
Numerator (my bracketing): 2[(q−1)+qp−q] = 2(pq−1).
Denominator: 3[p(q−1)+q(p−1)] −(q−1) −(p−1) = 6pq−3p−3q−q+1−p+1 = 6pq−4p−4q+2.
Hence pp = qq ss + (2pq−2)/(6pq−4p−4q+2) = qq ss + (pq−1)/(3pq−2p−2q+1).
The factor cc of (1) is no longer written. Either c is tacitly normalised to 1 or it was dropped.

B. Condition (2).
Using α+β = γ+δ (so β = γ+δ−α), Gauss notes (α−β)²−(γ−δ)² = (2α−2γ)(2α−2δ) = 4(α−γ)(α−δ). This is written over the formula.
He rewrites (2) as γγ/αα + (ββ/δδ)ss = 2{(α−β)²−(γ−δ)²}((γ−δ)²−(α−β)²ss) / [(α−β)(δ+3γ)+(δ−γ)(α+3β)]. Struck-out first attempts appear inside the brackets.
The marginal labels (δ−γ)n, (β−α)n, '1−n 3+n', '1+n 3−n' suggest he was trying to split the denominator with a free parameter n, i.e. (α−β)((1±n)δ+(3∓n)γ)+... . This is not carried through.
In p,q he writes pp+qq ss = (αα+δδqq−2αδp)/(ααp+αδ+δδq−3αδpq)·((αp−δ)²−(α−δq)²ss). This is a faithful substitution of (2) as written on the previous page.
He then inserts α → q−1, δ → p−1 (allowed up to a common factor, since α(p−1) = δ(q−1)). For the first numerator factor he writes (q−1)²+(p−1)²−2(q−1)p, and expands it correctly to pp+qq−2q+2−2pq.

C. Theta series (written vertically in the margin).
The series 1+2xx+2x⁸+2x¹⁸+... = Σ x^{2n²} is a theta series in x². Next to it is a condition of the form 2xx sin2φ + 2x⁸ sin8φ + 2x¹⁸ sin18φ + ... = 0, with fragments x⁶ sin2φ + x⁸ cos... .
This looks like the imaginary part of Σ(x e^{iφ})^{2n²} being set to zero. The precise intent is not recoverable.

D. Three conjugate values.
Gauss writes: '1/sqrt(M cos φ) hat 3 Werthe, deren Summe = 3/sqrt(M cos φ′)'. The sum of squares is given as 3/(M cos φ′)² (exponent placement ambiguous). He also mentions the 'Summe aus je zwei' (elementary symmetric function of pairs) and the 'Summen der Cuben' with a '+3' next to 3(1+2x⁶...)².
In the abstract notation the three values are written as roots of linear factors:
- x − P,
- x − εP − (1−ε)P′,
- x − εεP − (1−εε)P′,
with ε a primitive cube root of unity. Equivalently the roots are P′ + ε^j(P−P′), so the cubic is (x−P′)³ − (P−P′)³ = x³ − 3P′x² + ... ; Gauss writes x³ − 3P′xx.
The power sums he records are Σ′P = 3P′, Σ′P′P = 3P′P′ (sum of squares) and Σ′P³ = 3P′³. P′−εP = 1−ε is a normalisation; P+εQ, P+εεQ, PP+QQ is an attempt at a norm.
The concrete model is θ(x) = 1+2x²+2x⁸+2x¹⁸+... and its conjugate under x → (cube root of unity)·x, which he writes 1+2εxx+2εx⁸+2x¹⁸ (ε here standing for ε²; x¹⁸ is invariant).
The sum of the three conjugates keeps only exponents divisible by 3: 3(1+2x¹⁸+2x⁷²+...). This is the 'trisection' behind the order-3 relation between theta values.
He then multiplies θ(x) by its conjugate to obtain the coefficients needed for the sums of products and squares.

Purpose. To express the coefficient conditions of the cubic transformation in two parameters (p,q) tied to the modulus, and to identify the multiplier 1/sqrt(M cos φ) (a theta-constant/AGM quantity) with theta series whose three conjugate values have simple symmetric functions. This is essentially the modular equation of degree 3.
errors: Section A: the factor cc of condition (1) disappears in pp = qqss + (pq−1)/(3pq−2p−2q+1); presumably c = 1 is tacitly assumed, otherwise this is an omission.

Section B: the p,q form pp+qqss = (αα+δδqq−2αδp)/(ααp+αδ+δδq−3αδpq)·((αp−δ)²−(α−δq)²ss) is not homogeneous of degree 0 in (α,δ). The right side has degree 2 while the left side is a ratio. A normalising factor (e.g. 1/αδ or similar) must be missing, either here or already in the previous-page formula.

Section B: with α = q−1, δ = p−1 the numerator αα+δδqq−2αδp equals (q−1)²+(p−1)²q²−2(q−1)(p−1)p. Gauss wrote (q−1)²+(p−1)²−2(q−1)p, omitting the factors qq and (p−1). The subsequent expansion pp+qq−2q+2−2pq is correct for what he wrote.
Section D: Σ′P³ = 3P′³ is incomplete for roots P′+ε^j(P−P′). The true sum of cubes is 3P′³ + 3(P−P′)³. The marginal '+3' next to 'Summen der Cuben' may indicate he knew of an extra term.

Section D: the product (1+2x²+2x⁸+2x¹⁸)(1+2εx²+2εx⁸+2x¹⁸) is truncated/incorrect. The x⁸ term 2(1+ε)x⁸ and the x¹⁸ term 4x¹⁸ are missing, and the x¹⁰ coefficient should be 8ε, not 4(1+ε). The x², x⁴, x¹⁶ and x²⁰ coefficients are correct.
Section D: P+εQ, P+εεQ followed by PP+QQ — the norm (P+εQ)(P+ε²Q) is PP−PQ+QQ, not PP+QQ (unless a different meaning is intended).

results.what: Reduction of the coefficient/modulus conditions for the cubic rational transformation x = t(α+βt²)/(γ+δt²) to the two-parameter form pp = qqss + (pq−1)/(3pq−2p−2q+1), with p = γ/α, q = β/δ and α(p−1) = δ(q−1)
results.modern_name: Cubic (degree-3) transformation of elliptic integrals / modular equation of degree 3
results.usually_credited_to: Legendre (1825, Traité des fonctions elliptiques), Jacobi (1827–1829)

results.what: Three conjugate values of the multiplier 1/sqrt(M cos φ) via cube roots of unity; their sum is 3× the transformed value, related to the theta trisection Σ_j θ(ε^j x) = 3·(terms with 3|n)
results.modern_name: Trisection of theta series / symmetric functions of the conjugates in the cubic modular equation
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829); Gauss's Nachlass on theta functions and the AGM (c.1800–1818, Werke III)

results.what: Cubic with roots P′+ε^j(P−P′), giving x³−3P′x²+... and power sums
results.modern_name: Cardano-type parametrisation of the roots of a cubic

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's work on transformations of order 3, theta series and the AGM multiplier M is known from his Nachlass (Werke III/X) and predates Legendre and Jacobi. This page is a working draft of that programme with algebraic slips, not a new result.

Shows the correct substitution differs from what Gauss wrote (nonzero result)

checkable.asserts: Denominator αγ+αδ+βδ−3βγ in p,q form; should give 0

checkable.asserts: Power sums of the three roots: sum=3P′, sum of squares=3P′², sum of cubes=3P′³+3(P−P′)³; all should give 0
Correct product: coefficient of x**10 is 8e, x**8 is 2(1+e), x**20 is 4(1+e), x**16 is 4e

transcription_corrections: '2(p-1+qp' should read '2(q−1+qp', i.e. the numerator 2[(q−1)+q(p−1)] after substituting α ∝ q−1, δ ∝ p−1.
The label written vertically as 'x = 1+2xx+2x^8+2x^18' is better read as the theta series 1+2xx+2x⁸+2x¹⁸+...; the leading 'x =' is a separate marginal label.
In '1+2εxx+2εx^8+2x^18' the ε stands for the cube root of unity picked up by x² and x⁸ under x → εx (strictly ε²); x¹⁸ is invariant.
'Summen der Quadrate = 3/(M cos φ′)²': the exponent placement is ambiguous in the image; consistency with the other sums suggests 3/(M cos φ′).
In the struck term in '4 ε x^16' a symbol before x¹⁶ is crossed out in the image.
